title: Stretched-exponential finite-cluster tail wherever theta(p) > 0 (site percolation, d >= 3)
statement: Bernoulli site percolation on Z^d, d >= 3, C(0) the cluster of the origin. Conjecture 1.4. Let d >= 3. For any p in ]0,1[, we have the implication theta(p, Z^d) > 0 => liminf_{n -> infinity} (1/ln n) ln ln (1 / P_p(n <= |C(0)| < +infinity)) > 0. [Context: Theorem 1.2 of the source proves that at p = p_c either theta(p_c, Z^d) = 0 or that liminf is 0; the source says 'it could be that the correct way to prove that theta(p_c, Z^d) = 0 is to prove separately theorem 1.3 and conjecture 1.4'.]
status_search: Source (Cerf, 2026-08-22) states it as a conjecture; the campaign ledgers carry theta(p_c) = 0 itself (C0023, C0094) but not this tail statement. No other search run.

attempt.method: Split the conjecture by p. For p > p_c the supercritical finite-cluster tail is stretched exponential with exponent (d-1)/d (Kesten and Zhang 1990 for bond percolation, Grimmett's book Theorem 8.65; the site version follows the same Grimmett-Marstrand renormalisation), so the liminf is at least (d-1)/d > 0 and the conjecture holds there. The only case left is p = p_c with theta(p_c) > 0.
attempt.result: Conjecture 1.4 is EQUIVALENT to Conjecture 1.1 (theta(p_c, Z^d) = 0) modulo the supercritical tail theorem: 1.4 at p = p_c together with the source's Theorem 1.2 gives theta(p_c) = 0 (if theta(p_c) > 0 then 1.4 makes the liminf positive while 1.2 makes it zero); conversely if theta(p_c) = 0 the p = p_c case of 1.4 is vacuous and the p > p_c case is Kesten-Zhang. So the row is a reformulation of C0023 rather than a new target, and its only content beyond theta(p_c) = 0 is the site-percolation version of the supercritical tail bound.
attempt.obstruction: Nothing beyond theta(p_c) = 0 itself; the reformulation does not suggest a new route because Theorem 1.2 already consumes the tail information at p_c.
attempt.key_identity: theta(p_c) > 0 and Thm 1.2 => liminf = 0; Conj 1.4 => liminf > 0; contradiction

title: Second-order pivotal maximisers of increasing sets sit between Hamming levels n/2 - 2 and n/2 + 1
statement: Setting of the source's Part on pivots (Sections 47-58): for an increasing subset A of {0,1}^n, P^+_k(A, omega) is the set of pivots of order k of A at omega and phi_2(A) = sum_omega |P^+_2(A, omega)|, phi_{2 \ 1}(A) the analogous sum over second-order pivots that are not first-order pivots (formulas (51.1) and (52.1) of the source). Conjecture 53.1. Let n >= 1 be fixed. If A* is an increasing subset of {0,1}^n which realizes the maximum of phi_{2\1} or of phi_2, then { omega : sum_i omega(i) >= n/2 + 1 } is contained in A* which is contained in { omega : sum_i omega(i) >= n/2 - 2 }. [The source: the conjecture 'holds for n <= 7' by exhaustive search and 'yields a valuable upper bound' E|P^+_2(A)| <= 6 sqrt(n) for every increasing A; Section 59 tries Steiner symmetrisation and fails.]
status_search: Source states it as a conjecture verified only for n <= 7. Not in the earlier ledgers (no row mentions pivots of order two). No other search run.

attempt.method: Compare with the first-order analogue: for increasing A at p = 1/2, E|P^+_1(A)| = sum_i Inf_i(1_A) = 2 E[1_A (sum_i (2 omega_i - 1))] (monotone functions), which is maximised exactly by the majority set, i.e. the first-order maximiser IS a Hamming ball. Conjecture 53.1 asks the second-order functional to be maximised within two Hamming levels of majority.
attempt.result: The first-order statement is a two-line theorem; the second-order one has no such linear representation because a pivot of order two is a pair (i,j) with omega + e_i + e_j in A but neither single flip in A, a quadratic functional of 1_A. Sanity check: for A = majority with n odd, the second-order pivots at omega with sum = (n-3)/2 are all pairs of zero coordinates, of order n^2/4 per such omega, and the level has weight of order n^{-1/2}, giving phi_2/2^n of order n^{3/2}, not sqrt(n); so the bound E|P^+_2| <= 6 sqrt n quoted in the source must be read with the source's own normalisation of P^+_2 (which I did not verify in Section 51), and the row should be re-read against formulas (51.1)-(52.1) before any attack.
attempt.obstruction: Exact form of phi_2 (formula (52.1), a 708-page source) not extracted in this session; the magnitude check above disagrees with the quoted bound and must be settled first.

title: Deviations pivotal inequality for disconnection events
statement: Conjecture 58.2 (Deviations pivotal inequality). Let n >= 1 and let p in ]0,1[. There exists a constant c = c(p) which depends on p only such that, for a decreasing subset D of {0,1}^n which is of the disconnection type, we have for all k in {1, ..., n}: P_p(D) <= exp( -(c/k)/n * E[ |P^+_k(D)| | D ]^2 ). [Source: 'Conjecture 58.2, if true, would imply that theta(p_c, Z^d) = 0'; 'the case k = 1 of these conjectures has been proved rigorously in proposition 39.5 and corollary 40.3'; and, crucially, 'so far we did not succeed in defining properly a class of disconnection events for which the conjecture could be verified, which is why this concept is left intentionally vague'.]
status_search: Source states it. NOT ADMITTED: the hypothesis 'of the disconnection type' is undefined by the source's own account, so the statement has no truth value until a class is fixed; recorded so that a later reader does not re-mine it.
resolved_by: Not a resolution: excluded because the source leaves the hypothesis class intentionally undefined (Section 58, PDF p. 437). Re-admit if a later version fixes the class.

title: Increasing-events boundary-connectivity conjecture on finite graphs (implies theta(p_c) = 0)
statement: Bernoulli bond percolation with parameter p on a finite graph G = (V,E), o in V, B a subset of V. An event A is increasing with respect to the percolation configuration if omega -> P[A | pi = omega] is increasing on {0,1}^E (pi the configuration; the event may depend on extra randomness). Conjecture 2.2. There exists a universal function phi : (0, +infinity) -> R, independent of G, o, B and p, such that phi(eps) -> 1 as eps -> 0, and such that the following statement always holds. Let eps > 0. Let (E_b)_{b in B} be a family of events which are increasing with respect to the percolation configuration. Assume that P[E_b] >= 1 - eps for every b in B. Then P[ union_{b in B} ({o <-> b} cap E_b) ] >= phi(eps) P[o <-> B]. [Theorem 2.4 of the source: the conjecture implies theta(p_c) = 0 for every d >= 2, via Kozma and Nitzan's Theorem 6.]
status_search: Posted 2026-09-07; the source calls it its main conjecture. The earlier ledgers have no finite-graph connectivity conjecture (Kozma-Nitzan's is not there either, see G0005). No other search run.

attempt.method: Test the extreme cases. |B| = 1: {o <-> b} and E_b are both increasing, so Harris-FKG gives P[{o<->b} cap E_b] >= P[o<->b] P[E_b] >= (1-eps) P[o<->b], i.e. phi(eps) = 1 - eps works. General B: for the family of graphs where the connections o <-> b, b in B, are independent (disjoint routes) with common probability q, take the adversarial choice E_b = {o <-> B \ {b}}; then P[E_b] >= 1 - eps forces (1-q)^{|B|-1} <= eps and the union event is {N >= 2} with N ~ Binomial(|B|, q), whose failure P[N = 1] = |B| q (1-q)^{|B|-1} <= |B| q eps is at most eps log(1/eps) (1+o(1)) times P[N >= 1]; so on that family phi(eps) = 1 - O(eps log(1/eps)) works for this E_b.
attempt.result: Two supporting cases, no proof and no counterexample. The conjecture is strictly stronger than Kozma-Nitzan's Conjecture 3 (the source proves the implication), so it is at least as hard as that.
attempt.obstruction: A counterexample needs 'o connects to exactly one boundary point with high probability, uniformly over many candidates'; positive association of the connection events works against such concentration, and I could not build a Bernoulli example with P[N = 1 | N >= 1] -> 1 while every P[o <-> B \ b] -> 1.

title: Kozma-Nitzan high-probability connectivity conjecture on finite graphs
locator: proof of Theorem 2.4, Section 2, PDF p. 3 (restating Kozma and Nitzan, Conjecture 3)
statement: Bernoulli bond percolation with common parameter p on a finite graph G = (V,E). Conjecture (Kozma-Nitzan, Conjecture 3, finite constant-parameter form as restated by the source): for every eta > 0 there exists delta = delta(eta) > 0 such that, for every finite graph G, every A subset of V and every o, z in V, if P[o <-> A] > 1 - delta and P[a <-> z] > 1 - delta for every a in A, then P[o <-> z] > 1 - eta. [Kozma and Nitzan's Theorem 6: this implies theta(p_c, Z^d) = 0 for all d >= 2.]
status_search: Kozma-Nitzan's paper is cited by both Cerf (as [90]) and Flammant as very recent and unresolved. The earlier ledgers have C0138 (a different Kozma conjecture) only. No other search run.

attempt.method: Union bound with FKG. P[o <-> z] >= P[o <-> A] - P[exists a in A: o <-> a, a not<-> z]. For fixed a the event {o <-> a} is increasing and {a not<-> z} is decreasing, so P[o<->a, a not<->z] <= P[o<->a] P[a not<->z] <= delta P[o<->a]. Summing, P[o <-> z] >= 1 - delta - delta E[N_A], where N_A is the number of a in A joined to o.
attempt.result: The conjecture holds with eta = 2 delta (K + 1) on every instance where E[N_A] <= K: in particular whenever |A| is bounded, and more generally whenever the cluster of o meets A in a bounded expected number of points. The open content is exactly the regime where o's cluster meets A in many points, where the union bound over a is wasteful; what is needed is that the cluster of o, given it reaches A, reaches A at some point a whose own event {a <-> z} occurs, i.e. an FKG-type statement conditional on the cluster, which is Flammant's Conjecture 2.2 with E_a = {a <-> z}.
attempt.obstruction: No control of N_A in the interesting instances (boxes in Z^d with A a face: N_A is of order n^{d-1} there).
attempt.key_identity: P[o<->z] >= 1 - delta - delta E[N_A] (FKG on increasing x decreasing)

title: Is lambda_1 < lambda_p for the contact process on Z^d, d >= 2 (percolation of the upper invariant measure)
statement: Contact process with infection rate lambda on Z^d; lambda_1 the critical value for survival (lambda_1 = lambda_c on Z^d), and lambda_p the critical value beyond which the infected vertices of the upper invariant measure nu_lambda percolate. Source: '[8] proves in particular that ... lambda_p(Z) = +infinity, lambda_p(Z^d) <= 6.25 < +infinity for d >= 2. The same paper also raises the natural question whether we have lambda_1 < lambda_p on Z^d when d >= 2, which remains a difficult open problem. To the best of our knowledge, such a result has previously never been proven for any graph with lambda_p < +infinity.' The source proves lambda_1 < lambda_p on the regular tree T_d for all d >= 3 (and 0 < lambda_1 < lambda_p < lambda_2 < lambda_p^c < infinity for d >= 7).
status_search: Source (2026-09-09) calls it a long-standing open problem on Z^d. The earlier ledgers carry one contact-process row (E0007, two-type exclusion), not this. No other search run.

attempt.method: Read the tree proof for what breaks on Z^d: the source dominates nu_lambda from below by a product Bernoulli measure with parameter p_lambda and uses p_lambda < 1/(d-1) (the tree's site-percolation threshold) for lambda slightly above lambda_1; on the tree the branches below a vertex are conditionally independent, so a one-vertex density bound converts into a product-measure comparison. On Z^d there is no such conditional independence and the density of nu_lambda near lambda_1 is small (it vanishes continuously at lambda_c, Bezuidenhout-Grimmett), so the natural route is instead: show nu_lambda is dominated by a product measure of small density near lambda_c (which would give lambda_p > lambda_1 via p_c(Z^d) > 0).
attempt.result: No result; the sharper formulation is: does the upper invariant measure at lambda_c + eps stochastically dominate no product measure of density above p_c^site(Z^d)? A positive answer for small eps gives the conjecture, since 'dominated by' is the wrong direction for percolation but 'density of infected sites tends to 0 as lambda -> lambda_c' (continuity of the transition) plus a finite-range decoupling of nu_lambda would give non-percolation for lambda near lambda_c.
attempt.obstruction: nu_lambda has no known finite-range decoupling; its correlations near lambda_c are exactly the hard part.

title: Continuity of the two percolation transitions of the upper invariant measure on T_d
statement: Contact process on the regular tree T_d with upper invariant measure nu_lambda; lambda_p the percolation threshold of the infected set, lambda_p^c the threshold before which the healthy set percolates. Source: 'the figure suggests that both transitions are continuous, and it's possible as well that the probability to be in an infinite healthy component has a continuous derivative at lambda = lambda_p^c while the probability to be in an infinite infected component at lambda = lambda_p does not. We leave both questions as interesting open problems.' Question: are the functions lambda -> nu_lambda(0 in an infinite infected component) and lambda -> nu_lambda(0 in an infinite healthy component) continuous at lambda_p and lambda_p^c respectively, and is the first derivative continuous at lambda_p^c but not at lambda_p?
status_search: Source poses it (2026-09-09). Not in the earlier ledgers. No other search run.

attempt.method: Reduce to a percolation-in-random-environment statement: nu_lambda is a translation-invariant (in the tree's automorphism group) measure with positive association (it is the limit of an attractive spin system started from all-infected, so it satisfies FKG, Harris 1977). For FKG measures on trees, continuity of the percolation function at the threshold is not automatic; the standard route (Bezuidenhout-Grimmett style finite-size criterion) needs a finite-range or exponentially decaying dependence, and nu_lambda on the tree is a Markov chain along rays only in the Boltzmann sense, not a genuine finite-range field.
attempt.result: No result. First concrete sub-question: does nu_lambda have exponential decay of correlations along the tree at every lambda > lambda_1? If so, a Grimmett-Marstrand type argument in the tree setting would give continuity of the infected-percolation function at lambda_p.
attempt.obstruction: Decay of correlations of the upper invariant measure on T_d is not in the source and I did not find it elsewhere in the session.

title: Monotonicity of the two-point connection probability in the distance on Z^2
locator: Abstract and Introduction, PDF p. 1; Section 3, PDF p. 4
statement: Bernoulli bond percolation on Z^2 with parameter p. Source: 'on the square lattice is an open question to prove that the probability of the origin being connected to the vertex (0,n) is monotone in n' and, after the construction of a transitive graph without the property, 'it remains an open question whether graphs like Z^d satisfy the monotonic property or not'. Question: for every p in (0,1), is n -> P_p(0 <-> (0,n)) non-increasing on Z^2 (and on Z^d)? [The source traces the question to Hammersley and Welsh (1965) in first-passage percolation.]
status_search: Source (2026-01-01) calls it open; the transitive counterexample there is for a different graph. The earlier ledgers' 34 'monoton' rows are about other objects (checked by title). No other search run.

attempt.method: Check the trivial regimes. p small: P_p(0 <-> (0,n)) = p^n (1 + O(p)) with the correction from the number of self-avoiding paths of length n + 2k, so monotonicity holds for p below some p_0 by the connective-constant bound (number of paths of length m between the points is at most mu^m and the ratio of consecutive terms is p mu (1+o(1)) < 1). p close to 1: P_p(0 <-> (0,n)) = theta(p)^2 + (finite-cluster term) where the second term decays exponentially in n with a monotone leading behaviour; monotonicity for large n follows from the Ornstein-Zernike asymptotics of the truncated two-point function (Campanino-Ioffe-Velenik), which give C n^{-1/2} e^{-n/xi} (1 + o(1)) along an axis, so P is eventually decreasing for every p != p_c.
attempt.result: Partial: monotonicity holds for all n when p is small, and for all n >= n_0(p) when p != p_c (Ornstein-Zernike axis asymptotics at p < p_c, and at p > p_c via the truncated function). The open content is (i) all n at intermediate p, where exact enumeration to moderate n is the natural test, and (ii) p = p_c, where the two-point function decays as n^{-1/4+o(1)} on the triangular lattice and no monotonicity mechanism is known.
attempt.obstruction: No mechanism at p = p_c; at other p, uniformity of the Ornstein-Zernike error terms in n from n = 1 is not available.

title: Conditions for a giant component in supercritical percolation on a general finite graph
statement: Bernoulli bond percolation G_p on a finite graph G; lambda(G) the spectral radius of its adjacency matrix. Question 5.1. What natural conditions on G imply that if p >= (1 + eps)/lambda(G) then with constant probability G_p contains a component of size Omega(|G|)? [The source: 'the main difficulty ... is that lambda(G) can be governed by a very small part of the graph', with G possibly containing an induced subgraph H on (1 - o(1))|G| vertices with lambda(H) << lambda(G); the source determines the critical probability 1/lambda(G) for the emergence of a component of size comparable to the maximum degree.]
status_search: Source (2026-08-19) poses it. C0140 in the earlier ledgers is the transitive-graph giant-component question, a different setting. No other search run.

attempt.method: Identify the obvious sufficient condition and the obvious obstruction. Sufficient: lambda(G) attained by a 'spread' Perron vector, e.g. the vector v with v^T A v = lambda |v|^2 having ||v||_infinity^2 <= C |v|^2 / |G| (delocalised Perron eigenvector); then the expected number of vertices in large components is controlled by the same second-moment computation that gives the source's maximum-degree-size components, and a sprinkling argument of Krivelevich-Sudakov type should give Omega(|G|). Obstruction: a clique of size s attached to a path of length |G| - s has lambda ~ s and p = 2/s gives components of size O(s), so no condition weaker than 'the Perron mass is not concentrated on o(|G|) vertices' can suffice.
attempt.result: A candidate answer: delocalisation of the Perron eigenvector (||v||_infinity^2 <= C |v|_2^2/|G|) is necessary up to constants and plausibly sufficient; not proved.
attempt.obstruction: The sprinkling step needs expansion between the many maximum-degree-size components, which delocalisation alone does not give (a disjoint union of many small dense pieces has a delocalised Perron vector and no giant). So the correct condition must also bound the number of components at scale Delta, i.e. involve the second eigenvalue.

title: Tight subcritical bound on the largest component in terms of the maximum degree and the spectral radius
statement: Bernoulli bond percolation G_p on a finite graph G with maximum degree Delta(G) and spectral radius lambda(G), p <= (1 - eps)/lambda(G). Theorem 1.4 of the source: a.a.s. the largest component has size at most O( sqrt(|G| Delta(G)) log|G| / lambda(G) ), optimal when lambda(G) >> sqrt|G| (e.g. K_{s,s^3}) but not in all regimes (for lambda(G) = Delta(G) and G connected the true bound is O(log |G|)). Question 5.2. For a graph with given Delta(G) and lambda(G), what is the tight upper bound for the typical size of the largest component of G_p, when p <= (1 - eps)/lambda(G)? The source singles out the near-regular case Delta(G) <= (1 + delta) lambda(G).
status_search: Source (2026-08-19) poses it. Not in the earlier ledgers. No other search run.

attempt.method: Interpolate the two known ends. Regular: largest component O(log|G|) (branching-process comparison with mean p Delta < 1). Complete bipartite K_{s,t}, t >> s: components of size about s log s at p = (1-eps)/sqrt(st). A natural guess is that the answer is governed by the largest eigenvalue of the 'non-backtracking' or 'square-root-degree-normalised' matrix restricted to a subgraph: the size of the largest component is max over induced subgraphs H of (log|H|) / log(1/(p lambda(H))) up to constants, i.e. the subgraph that is closest to critical dominates.
attempt.result: A conjectural answer, no proof: largest component of order max_H log|H| / log(1/(p lambda(H))) with H ranging over induced subgraphs (for the regular graph H = G gives log|G|; for K_{s,t} the star K_{1,t} gives the t vertices of a star at p ~ 1/sqrt(st), consistent with the s log s scale only after the union over s stars, so the guess needs a multiplicity term).
attempt.obstruction: The multiplicity term (how many near-critical subgraphs there are) is what the source's log|G| factor hides; no clean formulation reached.

title: Long cycles in supercritical percolation on graphs of average degree d (Krivelevich-Samotij)
locator: Conjecture 5.3, Section 5, PDF p. 20 (restating Krivelevich-Samotij [28], see also [15])
statement: Conjecture 5.3 ([15, 28]). For every eps > 0 there exist d_0, gamma > 0 such that the following holds. If G is a graph of average degree d >= d_0 and p >= (1 + eps)/d, then G_p contains a cycle of length at least gamma d a.a.s. as |G| -> infinity. [Known: for d-regular G, Krivelevich-Sudakov give a path of length Omega(d) and Krivelevich-Samotij a cycle of length Omega(d); for average degree d and p >= C/d, [10] gives a cycle of length (1 - gamma) d with gamma -> 0 as C -> infinity; the source suggests combining its techniques with [10].]
status_search: Source (2026-08-19) restates it as open. Not in the earlier ledgers (no Krivelevich row). No other search run.

attempt.method: Reduce to a minimum-degree statement by the standard subgraph lemma: a graph of average degree d contains a subgraph of minimum degree at least d/2 (delete vertices of degree < d/2 one at a time). On that subgraph H, p >= (1+eps)/d = (1+eps)/(2 delta(H)) is only half-critical for H's minimum degree, so the reduction loses the factor 2 that makes the problem hard: the cycle must come from the sparse-but-dense-on-average structure, not from a min-degree core. Second reduction: by the source's own theorem, p >= (1+eps)/lambda(G) already gives a component of size Omega(Delta) at least; since lambda(G) >= d (average degree), p >= (1+eps)/d is supercritical for the spectral threshold, so a large component of size at least the maximum degree exists; the gap is turning a large component into a long cycle, which for regular graphs is the Krivelevich-Samotij DFS argument.
attempt.result: Two reductions and no proof; the second identifies the exact missing step (large component => long cycle without regularity).
attempt.obstruction: The DFS/rotation-extension arguments need a degree lower bound on the explored subgraph; average degree gives none after the first deletions.

title: Alon-Peres conjecture: non-backtracking walks of length C sqrt(n) are rarely simple (minimum degree 3)
statement: Conjecture 1.5 (Alon-Peres). For any eps > 0, there exists a C = C(eps) such that if Gamma is a graph on n vertices with all degrees at least 3, and k > C sqrt(n), then for any edge delta, the probability that a length-k random non-backtracking walk starting with delta is simple is less than eps. [The source proves the fixed-degree (regular) case; 'one could also explore analogs of these statements for (non-backtracking) closed loops'.]
status_search: Source (2026-08-28) attributes the general conjecture to Alon and Peres and proves only the regular case. Not in the earlier ledgers. No other search run.

attempt.method: Look for the degree-inhomogeneous obstruction to the source's method. Its proof samples a 'plan' (a successor edge for every edge) and shows a simple plan has many deviations that must self-intersect, by an excursion reversal that is measure-preserving for the uniform non-backtracking step in a regular graph. With variable degrees the reversal changes the walk's law by the ratio of degrees along the excursion, which is the only place regularity enters; bounded degree ratio (max degree / min degree <= K) should therefore give the conjecture with C depending on K by the same proof.
attempt.result: Plausible extension to bounded degree ratio (not carried out); the genuine content of the conjecture is unbounded degrees (e.g. a few hubs of degree ~ n attached to a cubic graph), where a walk that hits a hub is sent to a uniformly random neighbour and the sqrt n scale competes with hub revisits.
attempt.obstruction: For a star-like hub of degree n the walk returns to the hub only if it re-enters through a neighbour, so hubs can make simple walks LONGER; a quantitative birthday bound in the hub regime is the open part.

title: Catalano-Lavenant conjecture: the diagonal couplings of the uniform law are farthest from independence
locator: Conjecture 1.1, Section 1, PDF p. 1 (restating Catalano and Lavenant [4, Remark 3])
statement: Conjecture 1.1 ([4, Remark 3]). Let lambda denote the uniform probability measure on [0,1]. Then the diagonal and antidiagonal couplings (id,id)_# lambda and (id, 1 - id)_# lambda maximize the 2-Wasserstein distance from the independent coupling lambda (x) lambda among all elements of Pi(lambda, lambda). [The source proves the Gaussian analogue for all n: the couplings Law(Z, ..., +-Z) maximise W_2^2(gamma_n, .) over Pi_n(gamma), via the Gaussian isoperimetric inequality; the uniform case 'remains open to the best of our knowledge'.]
status_search: Source (2026-09-09) says open. Not in the earlier ledgers (no Wasserstein-dependence row). No other search run.

attempt.method: Write the objective as a maximisation of a supremum over transport plans: W_2^2(pi, lambda(x)lambda) = int |x|^2 dpi + int |y|^2 d(lambda(x)lambda) - 2 sup_{T in Pi(pi, lambda(x)lambda)} int <x,y> dT, and the first two terms are constant over Pi(lambda,lambda) (marginals fixed). So the conjecture says the diagonal coupling MINIMISES the maximal correlation sup_T int <x,y> dT with the product measure, over couplings of two uniforms. For the diagonal coupling this maximal correlation is that of the uniform law on the diagonal segment against the uniform law on the square, which is computable (the optimal map projects the square onto the diagonal monotonically along the direction (1,1)): value 1/2 + 1/12 ... (not computed to the end in this session).
attempt.result: A reformulation only: the conjecture is a MINIMISATION of the maximal correlation with the product law over bivariate copulas. The Gaussian proof uses that the extremal set is determined by an isoperimetric inequality; the analogous tool for the square is the (known) isoperimetric profile of the cube, which suggests the same proof scheme could go through for the uniform law, with the diagonal replacing the Gaussian half-space extremals.
attempt.obstruction: The Gaussian argument's key step (a Gaussian isoperimetric bound for the correlation functional) has no obvious uniform analogue with the right extremal set; not attempted further.

title: Bramson correction for the front of threshold cascades on unimodular random trees
statement: Threshold cascades of interacting diffusions on unimodular random trees, in the setting of the source's Theorem 2.1 (supercritical branching-random-walk representation with tilt parameter theta*, speed c*, derivative martingale dW_n). Conjecture 3.2 (Uniform integrability of the derivative martingale => Bramson delay). Under the hypotheses of Theorem 2.1, the derivative martingale dW_n is uniformly integrable (equivalently, dW_infinity > 0 a.s. on survival), and consequently the time-indexed front obeys F(t) = c* t - (3/(2 theta* c*)) log t + O_P(1), with the tightness and the limiting law of the recentred front given by a randomly-shifted Gumbel decorated point process, the shift being a multiple of log dW_infinity, exactly as for branching Brownian motion. [Source's Programme 3.3 lists the three ingredients, of which the x log^2 x moment condition for the offspring point process is the missing one.]
status_search: Source (2026-08-21) states it as the missing step of its Bramson programme. Not in the earlier ledgers (D0064 is the star-scale-invariance equation, a different object). No other search run.

attempt.method: Check the source's own reduction. Uniform integrability of the derivative martingale of a branching random walk holds if and only if the offspring point process satisfies the x log^2 x condition (Biggins-Kyprianou, Aidekon; Chen 2015 for the 'if and only if'), under the boundary case normalisation. So the conjecture's first half is a theorem the moment the cascade's offspring point process is shown to have E[X log_+^2 X] < infinity with X = sum over children of e^{theta* displacement}; the source's 'exponential-moment hypothesis on the offspring count' gives this directly when the displacements are bounded (then X <= N e^{theta* M} and E N log^2 N < infinity follows from the exponential moment).
attempt.result: Under bounded displacements the first half (uniform integrability) follows from known results plus the source's exponential-moment hypothesis; the second half (Bramson delay and the decorated Gumbel limit) then needs the Aidekon / Madaule programme for branching random walks with the cascade's spine structure, which the source says is available from its [1, App. A]. If the displacements are unbounded the x log^2 x condition needs a separate tail estimate.
attempt.obstruction: I did not read Theorem 2.1's hypotheses to confirm whether displacements are bounded; the row's status depends on that one check.

title: Continuum-random-tree scaling limit of the critical cascade cluster with a continuous type space
statement: Conjecture 7.2 (Continuous-type CRT scaling limit). Under the hypotheses of Theorem 6.1 at criticality rho(K) = 1, with the additional exponential-moment hypothesis on the offspring count (as in [1, Thm. 6.4]), the critical cluster conditioned on {|S| = n}, with graph distance rescaled by Sigma_c / sqrt n, converges in the Gromov-Hausdorff-Prokhorov sense to Aldous' Continuum Random Tree, with an explicit constant Sigma_c built from sigma^2_off and the tilted stationary law varpi*. [Source's Programme 7.3: the obstacle is that the type space is the Polish space R (or D x R), not finite, so Miermont's finite-type invariance principle does not apply directly; the missing input is a tightness estimate uniform in the discretisation mesh.]
status_search: Source (2026-08-21) states it. Not in the earlier ledgers. No other search run.

attempt.method: Route around Miermont. For multitype Galton-Watson trees with a general (Polish) type space and a spectral gap for the mean-offspring kernel, the CRT limit can be obtained from the Lukasiewicz-path / height-process route of the single-type theory by projecting types away: the total-progeny walk is a Markov additive process with finite variance under the spectral-gap assumption, and de Raphelis (2017, 'Scaling limit of multitype Galton-Watson trees with infinitely many types') already handles infinitely many types under a spectral-gap/moment condition, giving the CRT with an explicit constant; the conjecture's constant Sigma_c should match his.
attempt.result: A literature route (de Raphelis 2017) that appears to cover the conjecture's setting, which would make the conjecture a corollary once the cascade cluster is written as a multitype Galton-Watson tree with the source's kernel K. Not verified against the source's exact hypotheses in this session.
attempt.obstruction: de Raphelis's conditions (a Doeblin-type condition on the type kernel and moment bounds) must be checked against K; the 'D x R' type space with a diffusion coordinate may fail the Doeblin condition.
